facts.title: pickled carrot sticks
ingredients: 1 pound (455 grams) carrots, trimmed, peeled or scrubbed, and cut into 3 1/2- by 1/3-inch sticks
1 cup (235 ml) cider vinegar or plain vinegar (the former makes a sweeter, milder brine)
1 1/2 tablespoons dill seeds, coriander seeds, or black peppercorns, or a mix thereof
facts.cook_time: 15 minutes prep, plus 1 day or more to pickle
facts.author: Deb Perelman

steps.text: Place carrots in a heatproof jar you can store the pickles in. Bring remaining ingredients to a simmer in saucepan; simmer until sugar and salt have dissolved, about 2 minutes. Pour pickling liquid over carrots and cool, uncovered. Chill carrots, covered, at least 1 day for flavors to develop.
Carrots keep, chilled in an airtight container, 1 month.

Several 2024 Updates: I make these a bit differently than I did when I first shared this recipe from Gourmet [linked so you can go back to the original recipe if you miss it] 16 years ago, and have updated it accordingly. The changes: The recipe previously used 1.25 cups of water and 1 cup vinegar; I prefer these both at 1 cup. The recipe was much sweeter (with 1/4 cup sugar) and a bit saltier (with 1.5 tablespoons kosher salt); I use less of each these days. I also cannot resist using rainbow-colored carrot sticks but don’t advise it, regardless — the color turns the brine pink and the carrots all turn muddled and pink-ish, unless you’re into that! Finally, there’s absolutely no reason to limit your pickle flavoring to the dill seeds originally suggested, especially because they can be hard to track down. You can use coriander seeds and black peppercorns, or a mix thereof, as I do in these photos. Feel free to add slivers of fresh hot peppers for some heat, or even some fresh dill in the jar for more of a classic pickle flavor. Enjoy!
